major_concerns: Emulator/verifier fidelity to production networks is underspecified and may bias safety estimates.
Adversarial prompt-injection generation lacks a formal adversary model (adaptive vs nonadaptive) and may under/overestimate real attack success.
Single-LLM / single-verifier setup limits generality; results may not transfer across model/verifier choices.
One automated repair pass policy may be insufficient and needs justification relative to operational practice.
Statistical power/sample-size justification for paired McNemar analyses is not provided.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact hosted LLM model(s) and version(s) and justify choice; include plan for multi-model sensitivity or explicitly bound claims to tested model(s).
Define adversary threat model formally (capabilities, adaptivity, generation procedure) and provide representative attack-generation algorithm and examples.
Fully document verifier selection and configuration (Batfish/HSA settings, topology abstractions) and validate emulator fidelity against a small set of ground-truth device configs.
Add formal sample-size/power calculation for primary outcome and adjust dataset size or analysis plan accordingly.
Clarify retry/seed policy and justify single-repair-pass limit; if operationally motivated, document rationale in preregistration.

major_concerns: Simulation of registry signing and key-management is simplified and may overstate field effectiveness.
Adaptive adversary modeling is underspecified; 'adaptive-with-feedback' needs precise protocol and limits.
Definition of 'malicious tool' and realistic tool semantics are not fully described (could bias success labels).
Planner LLM behavior (prompting, temperature, chain-of-thought) not specified, affecting reproducibility.
required_design_repairs: Specify realistic key-management model for signing/attestation (including certificate/rotation assumptions) or explicitly bound simulation assumptions.
Formalize attacker adaptivity protocol with iteration budget, feedback channel, and scoring function; include example attacks.
Define tool semantics and malicious-tool behaviors concretely; provide canonical tool API/schema used in registry and rationale.
Document planner prompt templates, LLM settings (temperature, top_p), and seeding; preregister defense evaluation scripts and random seeds.

major_concerns: Three-run repetition may be insufficient to characterize API latency variance and nondeterminism.
Superlinearity claims require clear regression specifications and model-selection criteria.
Device models in the emulator may not reflect vendor-specific complexity; external validity risk.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact constrained-decoding implementation (e.g., lexical constraints, decoding algorithm, library/API) and how constraints are derived from intents.
Increase repetition count or use bootstrap/resampling to better estimate latency variance from hosted LLM API; preregister latency measurement protocol.
Predefine regression models, model-selection tests, and criteria for declaring superlinearity; preregister fit diagnostics.
Describe device-model fidelity and provide at least one validation case showing emulator produces expected verification traces versus a ground-truth config.

major_concerns: Scope is ambitious for a single short-paper run and risks becoming an under-specified dataset release rather than a focused experimental contribution.
Ground-truth for propagation/attribution is nontrivial to generate; labeling methodology is not defined.
Claims such as >75% attribution precision appear arbitrary without pilot data or conservative bounds.
Benchmark scenarios may be gamed unless diversity and adversary constraints are carefully designed.
Public release plan (licensing, hosting) and ethical considerations for adversarial scenarios are unspecified.
required_design_repairs: Narrow benchmark scope (fewer scenario types or smaller provenance graph depth) to match resource/time constraints and support a focused five-page paper.
Specify and operationalize ground-truth generation for propagation/attribution (deterministic scripts, injected faults with known root cause) and labelling process.
Replace fixed performance thresholds (e.g., >75%) with pilot-based target ranges or remove target guarantees; preregister evaluation criteria and success thresholds.
Define scenario diversity taxonomy and adversary-generation constraints to reduce gaming risk; include randomized scenario seeds and holdout set.
Document public-release plan (repository, license), anonymization/safety review for adversarial content, and reproducibility artifacts (seeded harness, hashes).
